details: October's core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation rose to 3.3% year-over-year, exceeding the 3.2% consensus forecast and marking its highest level since November 2023. This hotter-than-expected inflation data strengthens expectations that the Federal Reserve will maintain a restrictive monetary policy, dampening hopes for December rate cuts. The news contributed to a decline in Bitcoin and broader cryptocurrency markets, as higher interest rates typically increase the opportunity cost of holding risk assets.
title: US PCE Inflation Hits 3.3%, Fuels Fed Rate Hike Bets

details: Finance and central bank deputies from ASEAN+3 member countries (China, Japan, South Korea, and ASEAN) met in Kyoto and agreed to establish a dedicated working group on cross-border digital payments and digital asset regulation. This initiative aims to deepen policy discussions on retail and wholesale payment connectivity and regulatory approaches to crypto assets, including stablecoins, reflecting a growing regional focus on exploring and testing tokenization and stablecoin initiatives.
title: ASEAN+3 Nations Form Crypto & Digital Payments Working Group

details: Bitcoin faces potential selling pressure and increased volatility as the Federal Reserve's communication blackout period commences, limiting public comments from officials until December 10 and fostering market uncertainty. Concurrently, approximately $6.8 billion in Bitcoin options are set to expire on Deribit on Friday, November 27, which could trigger significant price swings as traders adjust positions. Defensive put options at various price levels indicate that traders are hedging against potential downside risks.
title: Bitcoin Volatility Feared as Fed Blackout & $6.8B Options Loom

details: The circulating supply of USDT has decreased to $81.1 billion, representing its largest decline since August 2022. This reduction is primarily attributed to activity on the Ethereum network and significant token burns by Tether. A shrinking USDT supply limits the liquidity available for cryptocurrency purchases, a factor historically correlated with downward pressure on Bitcoin's price and signaling cautious market conditions, often leading to declines in broader crypto market capitalization and DeFi locked value.
title: USDT Supply Shrinks, Signalling Crypto Liquidity Concerns

details: US spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) have experienced substantial outflows throughout November, with reports indicating nearly $5 billion in net withdrawals for the month. On one particular day, outflows reached $570 million, marking a fifth consecutive day of redemptions. This sustained institutional selling pressure, notably from major funds, is a significant contributor to the current bearish sentiment and price declines observed in the cryptocurrency market.
title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Face Record Outflows in November
